draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Munnar! Three rivers meet here, which is where the name comes from: 'moonu aar', three rivers. Every hill you see is stitched with tea bushes, planted by hand since the 1880s.
draft.hungryLine: Munnar runs on tea and something fried to go with it. Here's where to get both.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Start at the Tea Museum to see how the leaves are processed, then drive up to Eravikulam to meet the Nilgiri tahr.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Find a bench above Mattupetty Dam, order a hot chai and watch the mist roll over the water.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Anamudi, the peak you see from Eravikulam, is the highest point in India south of the Himalayas.

legends.title: A flower that waits twelve years
legends.body: Neelakurinji covers these hills in blue once every twelve years. The last big bloom was in 2018, so the next is due around 2030.

legends.title: The railway that a flood took
legends.body: A little railway once carried tea down these hills. The great flood of 1924 washed it away, and it was never rebuilt.

tips.title: Pack a jacket.
tips.body: Mornings can drop below 10°C, even when Kochi is sweating.

tips.title: Buy tea at the factory outlets.
tips.body: Fresher and cheaper than the shops on the highway.

story.title: Forests and the Muthuvans
story.body: Before any tea, these hills were thick shola forest. The Muthuvan people lived here, and legend says they carried their kings' children up into these hills on their backs.

story.title: A planter arrives
story.body: John Daniel Munro, a British resident, leased this land from the Raja of Poonjar. Within a few years, planters were clearing slopes for coffee and then for tea.

story.title: A tea town grows
story.body: Factories, a ropeway and even a small railway moved the leaves. Munnar became one of the biggest tea districts in South India.

story.title: The great flood
story.body: Monsoon rains in Malayalam year 1099 flooded the valley and swept away the railway. People here still call it the flood of '99.

story.title: Your turn
story.body: Walk a tea trail early, when the pickers start. Then come down for a hot chai and a banana fritter. Tell me if you spot a tahr.
